text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Stronger Treasuries pulled Bunds higher on Thursday, but as was the case for much of the week, German debt underperformed the U.S. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.64, up 0.16 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended in the red on Thursday, hit by fears over pension costs under a single European currency and edgy ahead of key U.S. jobs data. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-12/32, down 5/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures benefited on Friday from a virtuous combination of weak unemployment figures, an intervention rate cut and European Union acceptance of the French government plan to reduce its 1997 public deficit. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.44 up 0.22 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures surged ahead after Wednesday's late sell-off, lifted by lira strength against the mark, as the market settled down for what was expected to be a fairly uneventful day ahead of the All Souls' long weekend. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.53 up 0.83 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened higher on Thursday in front of weekly jobless claims data and September personal income and spending figures. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-21/32, up 2/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.69 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures contract ended the Tokyo session at 125.48 on Thursday, the highest level ever for any benchmark futures contract listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. The rally was led by speculative purchases by dealers. Some cash bond buying by institutional investors was also detected. The December ended at the day's high of 125.48, after opening at 125.12. It closed at 125.19 on Wednesday. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.37, up 0.25 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - A welter of paper hit the primary market on Thursday morning in a range of currencies and structures with Colombia's 275 million mark FRN standing out.
A syndicate official at joint lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said European institutions had been quick to snap up the five-year Colombian offering.
